chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman al-Daylami, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a group of thieves who had stolen. So he cut their hands from the middle of the palm, and left the thumb and did not cut it. He ordered them to enter the guest house and ordered that their hands be treated. So they were fed butter, honey, and meat until they were cured. Then he called them and said: 'O you all! Your hands have preceded you to the Fire. So if you repent, and Allah knows from you the sincerity of the intention, Allah will turn towards you (with Mercy) and your hands will join you in Paradise. And if you do not desist and do not stop from what you are upon, your hands will drag you into the Fire.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) punish thieves and what was the spiritual significance of the punishment?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic nuance of cutting the hand from the 'middle of the palm' (mid-karkh) rather than the wrist, a detail often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the precise definition of the amputation site. Imam al-Baqir (AS) uses this incident to illustrate the concept of 'sabaq al-yad' (precedence of the hand), emphasizing that the physical act of theft creates a spiritual trajectory toward Hellfire, which can be reversed through sincere repentance (tawbah) and divine mercy. The emphasis on nourishing the thieves with ghee, honey, and meat underscores the holistic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt, combining strict justice with compassionate care to facilitate spiritual healing.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman Al Daylami, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with a group who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> cut their hands from half the palm, and left the thumb and did not cut it, and ordered them that they should enter the guest house, and ordered for the healing of their hands. So they were fed the butter, and the honey, and the meat, until they were cured. So he<sup>asws</sup> called them over and said: ‘O you all! Your hands have preceded you to the Fire. So if you were to repent, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Knows from you the sincerity of the intention, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Trun towards you (with Mercy) and your hands would join you in the Paradise. And if you do not improve and do not stop from what you are upon, your hands would drag you into the Fire’.
